fields.name: Jeff Kolyer
biography: Crossover Stockton began with Jeff Kolyer, a former Silicon Valley technology founder exploring the transition from compulsory work to meaningful vocation.
After decades building technology, the question became personal: If machines can increasingly do the work, what are we free to become—and what will we do with that freedom?

fields.title: Street dogs and access to care
fields.description: Dogs are living on Stockton's streets. We don't know how many need help, what happens to them, or whether available services are reaching them.
fields.central_question: What happens to dogs on Stockton's streets, and what prevents them from getting the care they need?
fields.purpose: Understand the conditions dogs face, trace what happens when people seek help, and identify practical ways to improve access to care.

hero.headline: What happens when a dog needs help?
hero.subtitle: Dogs are being abandoned and found roaming Stockton's streets. We're examining what happens when someone tries to help, what care is available, who's providing it, and where access falls short.

fields.summary: Public reports describe roaming and abandoned dogs in Stockton. Animal Services reports shelter-capacity pressure, and organizations report feeding, fostering, and placement work. The number of dogs currently on the streets, their conditions, what happens after someone seeks help, and how reliably care reaches them remain unverified.
what_we_are_seeing: Stockton Animal Services reports recurring shelter-capacity pressure. It prioritizes sick, injured, aggressive, and confirmed abandonment cases, while healthy stray intake generally requires an appointment. Its guidance cautions that a roaming dog may be lost or owned rather than abandoned.
Stockton Street Dogs reports feeding and outreach on the streets several times a week. Its public materials also describe fostering, adoption, and other rescue pathways.

At an October 19, 2026 committee meeting, city officials discussed shelter limitations and repeated roaming-animal violations. The committee advanced proposed animal-control changes for full City Council consideration; the cited report did not establish a final Council outcome.
On October 20, Crossover requested Animal Services field-call records. They were received by email on November 2; their contents and limitations have not yet been assessed here.

San Joaquin County’s 2024 survey reported that 34% of unhoused respondents had pets. St. Mary’s describes pet-accommodating shelter options, but Crossover has not verified current access or whether people with dogs still face restrictions.
fields.current_state: Stockton Street Dogs reports that dumped-dog encounters rose from roughly one per week a year ago to about three to ten per week, with District 5 seeing notable activity. Stockton Animal Services reports recurring shelter capacity pressure. The current number of street dogs and how many reach safe placement remain unverified. Stockton Street Dogs is also pursuing a proposed Canine Campus for overflow, veterinary recovery, and volunteer-supported care; it is not yet an operating facility. People with pets may face shelter-access barriers; current access and dog-inclusive capacity remain unverified.

finding-new-facilities-impact-uncertain.title: Existing animal-care capacity is under pressure
finding-new-facilities-impact-uncertain.description: Stockton Animal Services reports recurring shelter-capacity pressure. The city is expanding its municipal animal shelter, while Stockton Street Dogs has proposed a separate Canine Campus intended to provide additional overflow, recovery, and care capacity. These efforts indicate that existing capacity constraints are an important part of the problem. How much additional care the facilities will provide, and whether they will adequately address unmet needs, remains unknown.

fields.title: Existing animal-care capacity is under pressure
fields.statement: Stockton Animal Services reports recurring shelter-capacity pressure. The city is expanding its municipal animal shelter, while Stockton Street Dogs has proposed a separate Canine Campus intended to provide additional overflow, recovery, and care capacity. These efforts indicate that existing capacity constraints are an important part of the problem. How much additional care the facilities will provide, and whether they will adequately address unmet needs, remains unknown.
fields.limitations: The evidence does not establish that the municipal expansion will be insufficient. The Canine Campus proposal does not independently establish the scale of unmet need or prove that the facility will be built. Actual future capacity and outcomes remain unknown.

stocktonia-2026-10-20-animal-control-pro.title: Committee advances proposed animal-control changes amid shelter overcrowding
stocktonia-2026-10-20-animal-control-pro.description: Stocktonia reports that on October 19 the Council Legislation and Environmental Committee advanced proposed changes addressing repeated roaming violations and a conditional fourth household dog or cat. Animal Services also described regular shelter capacity pressure, appointments for healthy stray intake, priority for sick, injured, aggressive, and confirmed abandonment cases, and a temporary found-animal foster pathway. These are reported practices and proposals; the ordinance still requires full City Council consideration before taking effect. For Dogs in Stockton, the report raises questions about how roaming dogs are classified, what happens after an intake request, and whether temporary care leads to verified outcomes. We are following Council action, foster eligibility and outcomes, and the pending field-call records request. The first street observation remains to be documented.

fields.description: Stockton Street Dogs / Street Dog Sanctuary proposes a campus for dogs without safe placement, including overflow and recovery care.
fields.intended_outcome: Increase safe dog-care and placement capacity, including space for dogs recovering from veterinary treatment.

capacity_summary.headline: Proposed capacity: Hundreds of dogs
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: Could provide overflow sheltering and recovery care for dogs waiting for safe placement.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Fundraising is documented; full funding, site, approvals, opening date, and usable operating capacity remain unverified.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: The proposal describes capacity for hundreds of dogs at a time; no funded or operating capacity is verified.

fields.demand_contribution: Could give dogs awaiting placement, shelter overflow, or medical recovery a safe care setting; none of that capacity is confirmed available.

milestones.description: Stockton Streetdogs opened a construction fundraising campaign for the proposed Canine Campus; this does not establish full funding or an operating facility.

open_questions: Has a suitable site been secured?
How much funding is committed, and how much is still required?
Are permits or other approvals needed, and have they been obtained?
Is there a realistic construction and opening timeline?
What would the initial usable capacity be?
What staffing and operating support will be required?
Which volunteer roles would be approved and actionable?
fields.next_verification_step: Request current project milestones, funding commitments and remaining needs, and site status directly from Stockton Street Dogs.

stockton-animal-shelter-renovation.title: Stockton Animal Shelter expansion
stockton-animal-shelter-renovation.description: City renovation and expansion of the Stockton Animal Shelter, including planned care and public-access improvements.

fields.title: Stockton Animal Shelter expansion
fields.description: City renovation and expansion of the Stockton Animal Shelter, including planned care and public-access improvements.
fields.intended_outcome: Improve animal care, veterinary facilities, and adoption access; the net change in dog placement capacity is not yet established.

capacity_summary.headline: Construction underway: Expanded treatment and recovery facilities
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: New treatment, isolation, and rehabilitation space could improve care and help dogs move toward adoption.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Completion, additional usable dog-care capacity, and effects on outcomes remain unverified.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: Planned medical, isolation, rehabilitation, adoption-lobby, and other facility improvements; additional dog-care places have not been quantified.

fields.demand_contribution: New treatment, isolation, rehabilitation, and public-access space could improve care and movement to adoption; net dog-place capacity and changed outcomes are unmeasured.

milestones.description: City scheduled a groundbreaking after awarding the construction contract; the later field visit confirms work proceeded.
Crossover field visit observed the expansion under construction; this does not verify completion.

open_questions: What construction work remains and when will it be accepted?
When will each new space open for use?
How many additional dogs, if any, can be cared for at once?
What staffing and operating resources are required?
fields.next_verification_step: Request the latest construction schedule and operational capacity plan from Stockton Animal Services.

fields.title: Pet Wellness & Adoption Center
fields.description: City of Stockton satellite animal resource center with Hard Luck Animal Welfare Advocates as a veterinary-services partner.
fields.intended_outcome: Expand access to veterinary, wellness, and off-site adoption services.

capacity_summary.headline: Facility development reported complete
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: Wellness care could help owners keep dogs, while off-site adoption space could help dogs leave shelter care.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Current services and measurable additional veterinary or adoption capacity remain unverified.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: City plans describe expanded veterinary services and a calmer off-site adoption space; current service volume is unverified.

fields.demand_contribution: Accessible veterinary care could prevent avoidable surrender, while off-site adoptions could help dogs leave care; actual incremental service volume is unverified.

milestones.description: City reported a grand-opening ceremony; this does not establish which services are currently available.

open_questions: Which wellness, surgery, and adoption services are currently available?
What are the hours, eligibility, appointment rules, and actual service volumes?
What additional capacity is attributable to this center rather than existing contracts?
fields.next_verification_step: Confirm current services, schedules, staffing, and completed procedures with Stockton Animal Services and Hard Luck.

fields.title: Animal Balance spay/neuter contract
fields.description: Separate three-month City contract with Animal Balance for high-volume shelter spay/neuter services.
fields.intended_outcome: Reduce the shelter sterilization backlog and shorten delays before safe placement.

capacity_summary.headline: City-approved contract target: Approximately 200 pets
capacity_summary.how_it_helps: Completed sterilizations could reduce treatment backlogs and placement delays.
capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Completed procedures, dog/cat split, and resulting care capacity remain unverified.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: Contract targeted approximately 200 pets across three clinic events; completed procedures and sustained capacity are unknown.

fields.demand_contribution: If delivered, additional sterilizations could reduce backlog and future unplanned litters; completed procedures and effects on intake are unknown.

procedure_tracking.period: Approximate target across three events under the three-month contract approved 2026-01-13

milestones.description: City approved a three-month Animal Balance agreement; delivery remains unverified.

open_questions: How many procedures were completed, by date and species?
Did the agreement clear any backlog?
Was capacity retained after the three-month term?
fields.next_verification_step: Obtain the Animal Balance contract performance report and reconcile planned versus completed procedures.

capacity_summary.not_yet_verified: Hiring completion and resulting care capacity remain unverified.

expected_capacity_or_benefit.description: Four additional contract positions were authorized; filled positions, procedure counts, and net capacity remain unknown.

fields.demand_contribution: Filled veterinary positions could expand treatment and sterilization throughput, reducing delays before placement; filled posts and output are unknown.

milestones.description: City approved a one-year extension and four additional positions; hiring and service delivery remain unverified.

open_questions: Were all four positions filled, and when?
Which services and locations gained capacity?
How many additional spay/neuter procedures or treatment appointments resulted?
fields.next_verification_step: Confirm staffing and service outputs with the City and Hard Luck, keeping them separate from Animal Balance totals.

location_type.label: Location type
location_type.description: What kind of physical place this is. It is independent of category, which classifies the evidence or source associated with the location.

map_reference.label: Geographic reference
map_reference.description: Public geographic search reference. Precision describes the query, not the accuracy of any associated report or the current location of a person or animal.

visual_description.label: Visual concept
visual_description.description: Optional subject or scene Crossover wants an independent renderer to understand; not alt text or evidence.

preferred_image.label: Preferred image
preferred_image.description: Optional preferred illustrative image path or URL; the renderer may use another image or none.

logo_description.label: Logo description
logo_description.description: Optional description of the record's authentic visual identity or symbol; not alt text.

preferred_logo.label: Preferred logo
preferred_logo.description: Optional preferred existing logo path or URL. Do not present an invented mark as an organization's official logo.

thumbnail_image.label: Thumbnail image
thumbnail_image.description: Optional thumbnail variant of the preferred image for compact displays.

description.label: Description
description.description: Stable description of the gap, distinct from its changing summary and story overview.

central_question.label: Central question
central_question.description: The question connecting the observed situation, unknowns, and work.

purpose.label: Purpose
purpose.description: What Crossover is working to understand and improve.

public_update.label: Public update
public_update.description: Marks an activity as a meaningful public development; visibility must also authorize publication.

organization_interaction.label: Organization interaction
organization_interaction.description: What Crossover actually did with or received from the linked organization. An application or inquiry is an outreach attempt, not acceptance or partnership. Use collaboration only when directly documented.

contact_activity_ids.label: Crossover contact activities
contact_activity_ids.description: Firsthand, occurred Crossover Activity records that identify this organization. A nonempty list means Crossover approached or heard from it; inspect each Activity's organization_interaction and outcome before claiming a response, visit, acceptance, or collaboration. Organizations without this field may still be referenced in research.

recorded_at.label: Recorded
recorded_at.description: When Crossover documented the activity in its records; this does not replace the event date.

occurred_at.label: Occurred
occurred_at.description: When the activity happened, independent of when it was confirmed, recorded, or published.

active.label: Active
active.description: Publication eligibility for the current Need index and related public updates. It does not describe whether the underlying condition persists or improves.

organization_ids.label: Organizations
organization_ids.description: Organizations related to this record. On outside evidence this is a reference, not evidence of Crossover contact.

map_reference_location_ids.label: Nearby geographic references
map_reference_location_ids.description: Nearby public geographic references for a task. These are not necessarily task sites or observed animal locations.

confirmed_at.label: Receipt confirmed
confirmed_at.description: When Crossover confirmed a previously received item had arrived; this does not replace the receipt date.

started_at.label: Started
started_at.description: When work on a task began; this does not imply completion.

parent_location_id.label: parent_location_id
parent_location_id.description: Canonical containing place for a facility; does not imply an event occurred at this facility.

canonical_location_id.label: canonical_location_id
canonical_location_id.description: Canonical place for a retained historical location record excluded from the top-level index.

facility_map_embed_url.label: facility_map_embed_url
facility_map_embed_url.description: Optional public Google My Maps embed URL for a parent place's facility map.

construction_contract_amount_usd.label: construction_contract_amount_usd
construction_contract_amount_usd.description: Awarded construction contract amount, supported by the initiative's funding source. This is a contract value, not operating capacity.

visualGuidance.preferredAssets: Preferred images and logos express a preference, not layout instructions. A renderer may use an appropriate alternative or no image.
visualGuidance.descriptions: Visual and logo descriptions describe an intended subject or identity; they are not alt text. Alt text must describe the image actually shown.
visualGuidance.evidence: Illustrative or generated imagery is not investigation evidence. Documentary images retain separate source, attribution, and caption information.
visualGuidance.logos: Do not present an invented logo as an organization's official logo.

imageDisclosure.scope: Do not place a generic image label over artwork or illustrations. Keep the image's origin, description, and evidence status in the feed. Site branding and navigation icons are excluded.
imageDisclosure.documentaryImages: When an image documents a real event or place, provide its source and context near the image. Do not treat artwork or generated imagery as investigation evidence.

browseGuidance.defaultView: Open browseable records with All types in one flat list, newest first by dateForSort.value. Preserve the mixed types unless the visitor filters or groups them.
browseGuidance.filtering: Search and type filters retain the same newest-first order. Put undated records after dated records; break equal-date ties by stable record ID ascending. Do not invent a date for an undated record.
browseGuidance.dateMeaning: dateForSort.field identifies what the date means. Event occurrence, receipt confirmation, documentation, publication, review start, completion, and verification are distinct. Label the selected field; never move an event date to the day it was recognized or recorded. dateForSort is a browse key, not a claim that every record was published or changed that day.

locationGuidance.presentation: For a Location with a nonempty map_reference.query, show a prominent Open in Google Maps link alongside its internal Crossover record link. Generate the URL from the query; do not store a duplicate URL on every record.
locationGuidance.precision: map_reference.precision describes the geographic search term, not a verified event, dog, person, or current condition. Corridors and general areas must be presented as broad references. map_reference.verified means the place name or address itself has a documented source; it does not verify associated reports.
locationGuidance.embeddedMaps: map_reference.embed_url is a Google Maps Share > Embed a map URL for a verified street address. Show it with the precision warning and Open in Google Maps link. Keep broad or unverified geographic references as search links rather than pinned embeds.
